A synopsis is still normative text. A reader could build attack/withdraw-only bookkeeping and miss no-attack entry or hazard-time participation, and a correct paragraph in another file does not automatically cure every contradiction.

independent_resolution: The specified contract explicitly assigns switching/entry to WP41 and growth to WP42 in WP39 purpose/non-goals and cross-references. WP41§4.2 unambiguously requires participation registration first, then hazards; an attack-only implementation would violate that existing required rule already. No newly missing entry obligation is demonstrated.

WP39 line192 gives nonexclusive historical-record examples and does not say only on those events, after damage, or one method call for every attack. Its interface context does not fix an implementation callback placement. Redundant maintenance during an attack/withdraw can be behaviorally equivalent when the history is already populated at entry.

The proposed ordinary no-attack growth observation therefore agrees with the complete contract. We preserve its source truth without turning extra precision or default callee placement into a new required ticket.

This is a finite interpretation judgment, not a claim the examples are well chosen or that all future positive contradictions are excused. If root independently identifies a normal observable mismatch against the combined rules, that separate exact premise can change the result.
